text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Parliament session ends with an attack by Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri who says people are harming the country and positive developments are not appreciated.
- Mortars fired from Lebanon land in north Israel early today.
- Lebanon's foreign ministry prepares to renew its request for international peacekeeping forces.
- United States embassy consul meets with prime minister to discuss the situation in south Lebanon.
- Lebanese Christian Maronite Patriarch Cardinal Nasrallah Sfeir says Lebanon is free of military war but is still facing economic pressures.
- Parliament deputies accuse the government of destroying the state.
- The secretary general of the Arab League has asked the Lebanese foreign minister to allow Iraq to compete in the Pan Arab Games which open in Beirut next week.
Lebanon has decided to exclude Iraqi athletes from the Pan Arab Games, sources close to the games said.
- The secretary general of the Arab League will visit Beirut tommorrow.
- Central bank looses $950 million in first nine months of 1997 due to price changes of gold.
- Prime Minister Hariri to visit Australia soon.
